title: Word Break
statement: Return true when `s` can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of dictionary words. The same word may be reused.
hints: A plain recursion tries every dictionary word at the current index and explodes on overlapping prefixes.
Let dp[i] mean the prefix s[:i] can be segmented.
dp[j] is true when some i < j has dp[i] and s[i:j] is in the dictionary. dp[0] is true.

approaches.name: Recursion without memory
approaches.explanation: Recomputes the same suffix many times.

approaches.name: Boolean prefix DP
approaches.explanation: One boolean per prefix, dictionary lookup per slice.

editorial: Put the dictionary in a set. dp[0] = True represents the empty prefix. For each end j, try every start i < j and set dp[j] when dp[i] and the slice is a word. The answer is dp[len(s)]. Memoized search is the same recurrence written from the other end.
